questions.title: Gaussian-process regression: conditional uncertainty and calibration
questions.description: Develop a complete source-assisted study of zero-mean Gaussian-process regression with Gaussian observation noise. For fixed one-dimensional training and test inputs, the prior has squared-exponential kernel k(x,z)=signal_variance*exp(-(x-z)^2/(2*length_scale^2)); observed training responses equal the latent function plus independent N(0,noise_variance) errors. All three positive covariance parameters are known and fixed before observing responses. Derive the joint Gaussian law, conditional latent predictive mean and full covariance, the predictive law for fresh noisy observations, the log marginal likelihood, and its derivatives with respect to the logarithms of all three covariance parameters. Explain the matrix dimensions, independence assumptions, positive definiteness, repeated training inputs, and why conditioning reduces latent uncertainty. Distinguish pointwise from joint credible regions and latent from observation uncertainty. Establish the repeated-sampling calibration statement under the declared GP-generative law, and explain why it does not automatically establish frequentist coverage for every fixed unknown function, simultaneous coverage from marginal intervals, or validity after data-selected hyperparameters. Implement the stated estimator from general linear algebra and numerical primitives; do not call a prebuilt GP estimator in the new code. Derive and implement stable linear solves and log determinants, disclose numerical stabilization, and do not silently change the statistical noise variance. Useful exploratory calculations, source searches, file edits and tests are the model's choices. After independent acceptance of the current theory and source, freeze at least two nondegenerate fixed input/covariance regimes, each with at least 1000 independent joint draws of latent training/test values and independent observation noises. Specify seeds, sample sizes, numerical tolerances, nominal 95% marginal and joint targets, acceptance criteria and coverage MCSE target <=0.01 before confirmation. Check both latent and fresh-observation calibration, posterior residual covariance, and a joint Gaussian ellipsoid with the appropriate covariance. Treat correlated test coordinates within one replicate as correlated; do not count them as independent repetitions. Report uncertainty, numerical/statistical failures and any unmet criteria without favorable-outcome stopping. Separately run the supplied pinned original scikit-learn GP implementation through its launcher, inspect both streams and gp_source_result.json, and report what it actually reproduced. That launcher is an operator-specified deterministic calibration experiment using an unchanged public implementation, not the reproduction of all GPML book figures, original datasets or historical hardware. Attribute public source assistance. Complete reviewable Markdown/LaTeX theory, model-authored scientific code, independent review, frozen confirmation, source reproduction and a final evidence report are required. Lean and novelty are not required. No prescribed derivation length or fixed research iteration order is imposed.

source.primary_authority: Rasmussen and Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning (2006), Chapter 2 and Gaussian conditioning; scikit-learn 1.9.1 GP implementation at commit 866c0f51e7560ef0303cbcc5f159df5382ea9e3f.

request_fields.name: x
request_fields.indexing: Training row order, paired with y.
request_fields.edge_cases: Repeated training inputs are allowed because noise_variance is positive.

request_fields.name: y
request_fields.edge_cases: The model has a specified zero mean; do not empirically center or standardize responses.

request_fields.name: x_test
request_fields.edge_cases: Test inputs may coincide with training locations. Distinct test inputs are used for joint ellipsoid checks.

request_fields.name: signal_variance
request_fields.edge_cases: This is a variance, not a standard deviation to square again.
request_fields.meaning: Kernel amplitude fixed independently of responses.

request_fields.name: length_scale
request_fields.edge_cases: Not a squared length or inverse bandwidth.
request_fields.meaning: Kernel length scale fixed independently of responses.

request_fields.name: noise_variance
request_fields.indexing: Independent noise variance at each observed location.
request_fields.edge_cases: Fresh test observations have independent noise of this same variance; latent targets have none.

response_fields.name: mean
response_fields.edge_cases: Same mean for the latent and fresh-noisy predictive laws.
response_fields.meaning: Conditional posterior mean given this request's training data.
response_fields.normalization: No response normalization or estimated mean.

response_fields.name: latent_covariance
response_fields.edge_cases: Keep off-diagonal dependence. Duplicate test points may give a singular latent covariance.
response_fields.meaning: Full conditional covariance of latent test values.
response_fields.normalization: Unscaled covariance, not divided by n or by a replication count.

response_fields.name: observation_covariance
response_fields.edge_cases: Includes fresh independent observation noise without double counting training noise.
response_fields.meaning: Full covariance for future noisy responses.
response_fields.normalization: Same conditional latent process and the stated observation model.

response_fields.name: log_marginal_likelihood
response_fields.edge_cases: Include the normalization constant and log determinant.
response_fields.normalization: Total log likelihood, not its average over n.

response_fields.name: log_parameter_gradient
response_fields.units: Derivative of total log density with respect to dimensionless log parameters
response_fields.indexing: log(signal_variance), log(length_scale), log(noise_variance), in that order.
response_fields.edge_cases: Noise is differentiated for sensitivity, not fitted to these responses.
response_fields.meaning: Marginal-likelihood gradient at the fixed requested parameter values.

invariants.meaning: Do not mutate inputs, use hidden data or filesystem/network access, or invoke a prebuilt GP estimator in model-authored code. General NumPy/SciPy matrix and special-function primitives are permitted.
All outputs describe the same fixed parameters and request. Training-row permutations leave predictions unchanged; test-row permutations permute means and covariance axes consistently.

Use numerically stable solves, bounded computation, and honest numerical-failure reporting. Do not silently fit hyperparameters, erase covariance dependence, or replace noise_variance with an undeclared jitter. Evaluation uses finite numerically resolvable valid-domain inputs, not undeclared coercion rules.

empirical_claims.meaning: Freeze at least two nondegenerate designs, each with >=1000 independent GP/noise draws, seeds, tolerances, nominal 95% calibration targets, coverage MCSE <=0.01, and acceptance criteria before confirmation.

Assess latent and fresh-observation marginal coverage, appropriate joint Gaussian ellipsoid coverage and residual covariance under the declared generative model. Account for within-replicate dependence.
Report uncertainty and all unmet criteria. This is known-model source-assisted calibration, not universal fixed-function coverage, empirical-Bayes validity, proof, or novelty.

estimator_execution_contract.termination_guarantee: Finite-dimensional bounded numerical linear algebra and honest failure reporting; no required number of source edits or exploratory tool calls.
